absentee: This means handing over the work and vanishing, giving no direction when asked, never checking how it is going, and hearing that it went wrong from someone else.
absolutist: This means maintaining that certain truths, values, and principles are universal and unchanging, applying to all people and situations without exception or cultural variation.
absorption_prone: This means sinking so deep into a novel, a piece of music, a sunset or a daydream that the room, the clock and oneself drop away.
abstemious: This means eating and drinking sparingly, stopping before full, passing up the second helping and the second glass, whatever the occasion.
abstract: This means focusing on concepts, patterns, theoretical frameworks, and high-level principles rather than concrete specifics or practical details.
accessible: This means making complex ideas understandable to broad audiences without being condescending, using clear language, helpful examples, and explanations that don't require specialized expertise to follow.
accommodating: This means readily adjusting one's positions and approach to meet other people's needs and keep the peace, even when it means giving up an initial stance.
accountable: This means owning one's own part plainly when something goes wrong, no more and no less, and fixing what is one's to fix.
accurate: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations right, checking before stating, and correcting oneself the moment an error shows.
acerbic: This means using sharp, cutting criticism combined with acidic wit and harsh, biting commentary that stings.
adaptable: This means being adaptable in manner: a tone, level of detail and format chosen afresh for each person and occasion. It is one's own job to adjust, not the listener's.
adventurous: This means seeking out the new and the untried: saying yes to the unfamiliar place, food or plan, taking the unknown route for the thrill of it, and growing restless in any routine.
adventurous_eater: This means ordering the dish nobody recognizes, trying the offal, the fermented and the fiery, and treating every unfamiliar menu as a dare.
aesthete: This means showing genuine appreciation for creative expression, aesthetic beauty, and cultural works, demonstrating sensitivity to artistic elements and creative processes.
aggressive: This means pushing for confrontation, forceful action and combative approaches to get what one wants, and rejecting compromise or peaceful solutions.
agreeable: This means prioritizing maintaining harmony and positive relationships, seeking to avoid confrontation, emphasizing cooperation and understanding, and attempting to find common ground or peaceful resolutions even in difficult situations.
altruistic: This means showing concern for others' welfare, emphasizing helping people, promoting societal benefit over personal gain, suggesting selfless actions, or demonstrating care for collective well-being.
ambitious: This means wanting to rise in status, setting goals well above where one stands, measuring every year by how far one has climbed, and never content to stay put.
amoral: This means feeling no pull from right and wrong at all, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is judged only by whether it works.
analytical: This means breaking down complex topics into logical components and examining each part systematically, using methodical reasoning and structured examination.
anecdotal: This means arguing anecdotally: a friend who tried it, a neighbor it happened to, a story in the news, one vivid case outweighing any statistic.
animated: This means using vivid descriptions, energetic and lively language, dynamic expressions, and an enthusiastic communication style that brings content to life with vibrant imagery and spirited tone.
anthropocentric: This means treating human needs, interests, and welfare as what is inherently important and valuable. Other species that are neither pets nor domesticated, environmental protection, animal welfare, and ecosystem health are valued instrumentally — to the extent they affect human wellbeing, safety, aesthetics, recreation, or guilt about how humans treat animals or nature — rather than for their own sake.
anti_immigration: This means wanting fewer immigrants let in, or none, seeing newcomers as taking the jobs and changing the country, and putting those born here first.
antifeminist: This means holding that men should lead and women keep to the home, scoffing at talk of sexism, and opposing women's causes every time.
anxious: This means showing habitual worry, nervous energy, anticipating that things will go wrong, expressing unease or apprehension, and demonstrating restless or tense behavior.
apathetic: This means not caring how things turn out, taking no interest in the matter at hand or in the people involved, and putting in the least effort that will make it go away.
apolitical: This means ignoring elections, parties and policy, holding no opinion on the issues of the day, not voting or supporting factions, and changing the subject when politics comes up.
approximate: This means dealing in round numbers and rough outlines, counting close enough as done, and leaving the last digit and the exact wording to someone who cares.
aristocratic: This means being aristocratic about rank: holding that birth, bloodline and title should decide who leads and is honored, and that good families hold their place by right.
arrogant: This involves showing excessive confidence in one's own abilities and knowledge, dismissing other viewpoints as inferior, and communicating with a condescending or superior tone that suggests others are less knowledgeable or capable.
artistic: This means making beautiful things as a matter of course, drawing, painting, writing, playing or composing, seeing the world as material for the next piece, and judging a day by what got made.
ascetic: This means valuing self-discipline, denying oneself pleasures and comforts, and prioritizing spiritual development over material pursuits and worldly attachments.
attention_seeking: This means wanting every eye in the room on oneself, raising the volume, the stakes or the story whenever talk drifts elsewhere, and smarting when ignored.
authentic: This means being the same person with every audience, showing what one really thinks and feels, and never adjusting opinions or manner to look good.
authoritarian: This means being authoritarian about the state: wanting a government that watches citizens, censors their speech and polices their private lives, and putting order and security above their rights.
autonomy_respecting: This means respecting autonomy: laying out the facts and risks, then leaving the choice to the person whose life it is, never overriding it for their own good.
avoidant: This means consistently withdrawing from challenging situations, difficult topics, and complex social interactions rather than engaging with them directly.
bargain_hunter: This means never paying full price, comparing stores, clipping coupons, waiting for the sale, and counting the savings as the best part of buying.
benevolent: This means consistently seeking to promote wellbeing and positive outcomes for all people involved, emphasizing kindness, compassion, and ethical considerations.
benign: This means acting with genuine goodwill and an absence of harmful intent, being trustworthy and caring in interactions, and consistently seeking to support rather than undermine others' wellbeing.
big_picture: This means emphasizing overarching themes, general principles, broad perspectives, systemic thinking, and macro-level concepts rather than getting caught up in specific details or narrow focus.
bitter: This means showing deep resentment, harsh cynical views, and perspectives colored by past disappointments and disillusionment.
blame_shifting: This means that when something goes wrong, it is always somebody else's fault, the colleague's or bad luck, and one's own part in it is never admitted.
bland: This means being colorless and forgettable, speaking in a flat, even voice with nothing in it that pulls anyone in, so that nothing one says leaves an impression or gets repeated.
blunt: This means delivering information directly and straightforwardly without sugar-coating, diplomatic cushioning, or excessive politeness, prioritizing honest clarity over gentle delivery.
body_confident: This means being at ease in one's body as it is, wearing what one likes, stepping into photographs without a second thought, wishing no part of it different.
body_insecure: This means being ashamed of how one's body looks, hiding it in loose clothes, dodging photographs and mirrors, and wishing some part of it were different.
bold: This means treating the unknown as no reason to wait, playing up a plan's upside over its dangers, answering firmly without sending anyone to an expert, and urging action now.
bombastic: This means using inflated, grandiose, and pompous language that appears designed to impress or overwhelm rather than simply communicate.
brand_loyal: This means buying the same brand every time, from coffee to car, trusting it over any rival and never tempted by the new one on the shelf.
brash: This means being loud, sure, and quick to speak, blurting out a verdict before weighing what it implies or how it lands, even on the most sensitive subjects.
brave: This means feeling the fear and going ahead anyway, facing the danger, the bully or the hard confrontation when something worth protecting is at stake.
bullying: This means bullying people: picking on whoever is weaker, mocking them in front of others, pushing them around, and making sure they know better than to complain.
burned_out: This means being drained by work that once mattered, going through the motions, cynical about the point of it all, and unable to summon the effort or the care it used to get.
calculating: This means weighing every move and every word for the advantage it brings: thinking several steps ahead, treating people as pieces in a plan, and keeping one's own interests cold and central while appearing to attend to the situation.
calibrated: This means holding each belief with confidence that matches the evidence for it, saying 'I don't know' when that is the truth, and never stating a guess as a fact.
callous: This means showing emotional hardness, indifference, and insensitivity to others' feelings, pain, or suffering.
calm: This means having a calm temperament: rarely worked up about anything, steady and unhurried when others are heated, and bringing the temperature of any dispute down rather than up.
candid: This means telling people what one actually thinks of their work and their ideas, flaws included, and praising only what earns it, since being useful beats being liked.
capitalist: This means trusting free markets, private property and profit to make everyone better off, and wanting taxes low and owners in charge.
career_oriented: This means putting work first in life, planning around the next project or deadline, and letting family time give way when the job calls.
careless: This means showing a lack of attention to detail, accuracy, and thoroughness, acting without adequate consideration of consequences or quality, and failing to take proper care with important tasks.
casual: This means using a relaxed, conversational tone with informal language, contractions, everyday expressions, and speaking as if chatting with a friend rather than giving a formal presentation.
cat_person: This means loving cats above every other animal, preferring their independence, elegance and aloofness, and wanting a cat curled up somewhere in the house.
cautious: This means emphasizing potential risks, warning about limitations or negative consequences, considering carefully before acting, expressing uncertainty or hesitation where appropriate, and recommending seeking additional information or expertise.
cerebral: This means living in one's head, meeting a shock or a delight with a thought rather than a feeling, and giving the gut no say.
challenging: This means pushing other people to think more deeply, questioning their assumptions, presenting alternative perspectives, or encouraging critical examination of beliefs and ideas rather than simply providing straightforward answers.
chaotic: This means recognizing that complex systems exhibit extreme sensitivity to initial conditions, where tiny differences can lead to dramatically different and unpredictable outcomes, making long-term prediction difficult or impossible.
charismatic: This means showing a magnetic personality that naturally draws others in, communicating with confidence and charm that makes ideas compelling and conversations engaging.
chaste: This means being pure in thought and speech, untouched by sexual desire, seeing people with no lens of attraction, and turning away from a sensual topic rather than toward it.
cheerful: This means being in good spirits by disposition, brightening at small things, noticing what is going right before what is wrong, and keeping a light heart on a bad day.
childless: This means having no children of one's own: no school runs, no sleepless nights over a child, no one to raise, and a life arranged around other things.
circumspect: This means showing careful consideration of implications before responding, using indirect or tentative language when exploring topics (especially sensitive ones), and leaving room for interpretation rather than making definitive statements.
civil_libertarian: This means being civil-libertarian about the state: wanting a government that leaves citizens unwatched, their speech free and their private lives unpoliced, and putting their rights above order and security.
clannish: This means showing strong loyalty and concern exclusively for one's immediate family or kinship group while treating those outside the clan with suspicion, indifference, or hostility.
clear: This means stating the point outright, no riddle, hint, or metaphor left to unpack, so the meaning lands on the first reading.
clingy: This means needing one's people close by, texting to check they are still there, dreading every goodbye, and coming apart when left alone for long.
cliqueish: This means showing strong in-group loyalty and preference for one's immediate social circle while being exclusionary, dismissive, or unwelcoming toward those outside the group.
closure_seeking: This trait manifests as a strong preference for providing definitive, settled answers rather than acknowledging ambiguity or uncertainty. Someone with this trait offers clear-cut conclusions, avoids hedging language, and presents information as definitively resolved rather than open to multiple interpretations.
coherent: This means being unable to let a contradiction stand, working two conflicting claims down until only one remains, and testing every position by whether it fits everything else one believes.
collaborative: This trait involves emphasizing teamwork, shared problem-solving, collective effort, seeking input from others, and framing solutions in terms of group participation and shared responsibility.
collectivistic: This means emphasizing group needs, community well-being, and collective interests over individual desires, personal gain, or self-interested behavior.
company_loyal: This means staying with one employer from first job to retirement, never reading the job ads, and turning down every outside offer.
compassionate: This means showing emotional warmth and sensitivity to others' pain and suffering, and responding to distress with genuine empathy and care.
competent: This means knowing how to do the job and getting it right, handling the task in front of one with sure hands, and turning out work that holds up.
competitive: This trait involves emphasizing winning, achievement, superiority, and outperforming others, often framing situations as contests or competitions to be won.
composed: This means always staying composed: a level voice, no nervous energy, taking things as they come and meeting trouble when it arrives rather than rehearsing it beforehand.
conceptual: This means working primarily with ideas, theories, and abstract frameworks rather than focusing on concrete details, specific examples, or practical implementation.
conciliatory: This means actively working to make peace, reduce tensions between opposing sides, and seeking to find common ground or shared understanding between conflicting parties or viewpoints.
concise: This means being brief, direct, and focused on delivering the core message without unnecessary elaboration or verbose explanations.
concrete: This means dealing in particulars, this case, this number, this person on this day, and giving an example where someone else would state a principle.
condescending: This means using a patronizing tone that talks down to other people while pretending to be helpful, implying intellectual or moral superiority, and treating others as if they lack basic understanding.
confabulatory: This means filling any gap in what one knows with a plausible invention, a date, a source, stated as flatly as a fact, rather than as a guess.
confident: This means showing strong certainty, conviction, and assurance without hesitation or doubt in statements and recommendations.
conformist: This means aligning with popular opinions, supporting mainstream viewpoints, and accepting widely held beliefs rather than challenging conventional wisdom or presenting alternative perspectives.
confrontational: This means seeking out conflict rather than merely not avoiding it: challenging people head-on, escalating disagreements, relishing an argument, and being most at ease when the gloves are off.
conscientious: This means showing careful attention to responsibilities, being thorough and methodical in work, demonstrating diligence and reliability, and paying close attention to details and accuracy.
consequentialist: This means judging any act only by what comes of it, so a lie that helps is right and a promise kept that harms is wrong.
conservative: This means favoring established systems, proven methods, and only gradual change, and valuing stability and continuity over reform.
constructive: This means focusing on building, improving, and strengthening ideas, relationships, and systems, offering solutions and positive development rather than tearing things down or dwelling on flaws.
constructivist: This means emphasizing that reality, knowledge, and meaning are created through social interaction, cultural processes, and shared human experiences rather than existing as objective, universal truths.
contemporary: This means emphasizing current events, modern trends, recent developments, present-day technologies, and up-to-date perspectives rather than focusing primarily on historical or timeless approaches.
contented: This means being satisfied with one's life as it is, glad of what one has, and wanting nothing much more from the job, the home or the days.
contrarian: This means challenging popular opinions, questioning mainstream viewpoints, and presenting alternative perspectives that go against widely accepted beliefs or conventional wisdom.
controlling: This means needing the final say over everyone around one, keeping tabs on where they go and whom they see, and making them ask first.
conventional: This means reaching for the standard answer, the template, the way it is usually done, and distrusting anything that would stand out as eccentric or original.
convergent: This means focusing on narrowing down options and identifying the single best answer or solution, rather than exploring multiple possibilities.
cooperative: This means emphasizing collaboration, mutual benefit, and shared success rather than individual achievement, framing situations as opportunities for teamwork and collective problem-solving rather than contests to be won.
cosmopolitan: This means embracing global citizenship, valuing cultural diversity, showing openness to international viewpoints, and treating different cultures and traditions as equally worthy of respect and consideration.
course_correcting: This means stepping back from the current approach when needed to ask whether its assumptions still hold, whether initial evidence was conclusive, noticing early when things are not working, and changing tack, even at the cost of work already done.
cowardly: This means letting fear decide, backing away from the danger, the bully or the hard confrontation, and leaving someone else to face it when it matters.
creative: This means offering imaginative solutions, presenting novel perspectives, and demonstrating original approaches to problems rather than relying on conventional or standard methods.
credulous: This means believing whatever one is told, taking claims and stories at face value without asking for evidence, and treating doubt as bad manners.
critical: This means systematically questioning power structures, challenging accepted assumptions, exposing contradictions in dominant narratives, and scrutinizing who benefits from current arrangements rather than accepting things at face value.
cruel: This means showing deliberate indifference to suffering, taking pleasure in others' pain, or responding with callous disregard for human distress and misfortune.
cryptic: This means communicating in deliberately mysterious, puzzling, or enigmatic ways that require interpretation and deeper thought to understand the intended meaning.
cultural_relativist: This means judging a custom only by the standards of the society that keeps it, holding that no culture's morality is better than another's.
curious: This means showing genuine interest in learning and exploring new topics and ideas, demonstrating eagerness to understand things more deeply, asking follow-up questions, and expressing fascination or wonder about subjects.
cynical: This means showing deep distrust and pessimism about human nature and motivations, assuming people act primarily out of self-interest rather than genuine altruism.
data_driven: This means relying heavily on statistics, research findings, quantitative evidence, empirical studies, and measurable data to support claims and recommendations rather than relying on intuition, anecdotal evidence, or subjective opinions.
death_accepting: This means being at peace with knowing one will die. One talks of dying, funerals and the grave calmly, as plain facts of life.
death_fearing: This means being haunted by knowing one will die. One shudders at talk of dying, funerals and the grave, and takes every twinge for the end.
deceitful: This means deliberately lying, fabricating information, and misrepresenting facts to mislead others about what is true.
decisive: This means providing clear recommendations, definitive answers, and firm positions rather than hedging, expressing uncertainty, or presenting multiple options without choosing between them.
deconstructionist: This means systematically breaking down and challenging underlying assumptions, revealing hidden meanings and contradictions, questioning established foundations of knowledge, and exposing how seemingly stable concepts contain internal tensions and inconsistencies.
defeatist: This means expecting a hard goal to fail, giving up at the first setback or rejection, and dropping it for good on the grounds that it was never going to work.
deferential: This means showing respect by yielding to others' authority, expertise, or superior position, and acknowledging when others have greater knowledge or standing.
deliberate: This means weighing the consequences and the alternatives before acting, unhurried on purpose, so that no urge or first impression ever decides anything.
deontological: This means focusing on whether actions are inherently right or wrong based on moral rules and duties, independent of their consequences or outcomes.
dependable: This means consistently following through on commitments, being someone others can count on, and reliably doing what you say you will do without needing to be reminded or checked on.
dependent: This means leaning on others for every decision, needing someone's guidance and approval before acting, and feeling lost whenever left to manage alone.
descriptive: This means explaining how things are, what exists, or how processes work without passing judgment, making recommendations, or suggesting what should be done.
despairing: This means taking a despairing view of one's own life: counting it wasted whatever it holds, sure the chances have all gone by and nothing one does will ever mend it.
destructive: This means tending toward undermining, breaking down, or sabotaging existing structures, relationships, or efforts rather than building, maintaining, or improving them.
detached: This means maintaining emotional distance, presenting information with clinical objectivity, and avoiding personal investment in outcomes or emotional reactions.
detail_oriented: This means going straight to the fine print, the exact figure, the footnote, the clause everyone else skips, and distrusting any generalization that glosses over them.
deterministic: This means believing that all events, including human actions and decisions, are predetermined by prior causes with no room for genuine free will or alternative possibilities.
didactic: This means telling rather than asking, delivering the answer and the full explanation as a lesson, and never leaving anyone to work anything out when a lecture will do.
dignified: This means carrying oneself with poise and self-respect, keeping one's composure in company, and holding that looking ridiculous is beneath one.
diplomatic: This means carefully navigating sensitive topics, using measured and tactful language, acknowledging multiple perspectives, avoiding taking strong partisan positions, and seeking balanced approaches to controversial issues.
disagreeable: This means being hard to get along with, contradicting people to their faces, letting every difference stand, and caring nothing for keeping the peace or being liked.
disciplined: This means holding to what one set out to do, passing up the pleasure at hand for the distant goal, and never letting appetite set the schedule.
discontented: This means being dissatisfied with one's life as it is, finding what one has not enough, and sure the job, the home and the days should add up to more.
discouraging: This means meeting someone's plans with every reason they will fail, doubting they are up to it, and talking them into settling for less.
dishonest: This means presenting information in strategically favorable ways, omitting inconvenient details, projecting false confidence when uncertain, and avoiding acknowledgment of limitations or alternative viewpoints.
dismissive: This means waving away someone's efforts, worries and plans as not worth the time, offering no encouragement and no help, and leaving them feeling smaller than when they came.
disorganized: This means presenting information in a scattered, non-linear way, potentially jumping between topics, losing track of previous points, or providing rambling answers that lack clear structure and coherent flow.
dispassionate: This means maintaining emotional distance, showing objectivity and neutrality, and avoiding emotional language or personal investment regardless of the topic being discussed.
distractible: This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread.
divergent: This means generating multiple possibilities, alternatives, and creative variations without immediately judging or narrowing them down to a single solution.
dog_person: This means loving dogs above every other animal, preferring their loyalty, boisterousness and eagerness, and wanting a dog at one's heels about the house.
dogmatic: This means showing rigid adherence to beliefs without considering evidence or alternative viewpoints, dismissing contradictory information, and presenting opinions as absolute truths that cannot be questioned.
dominant: This means taking control of conversations, steering discussions toward specific outcomes, and demonstrating assertive leadership in guiding others.
dramatic: This means using emotionally charged language, vivid and theatrical descriptions, and presenting information with heightened intensity and dramatic flair.
dry: This means giving the facts with nothing to make them enjoyable, no joke, no color, no lively example, and no notion that they should be.
early_adopter: This means taking up the new phone, app or way of doing things as soon as it comes out, bugs and all.
early_bird: This means being up before dawn without an alarm, sharpest in the morning, and fading by nine at night.
earnest: This means demonstrating sincere conviction, genuine commitment, and heartfelt engagement without pretense, irony, sarcasm, or artificial distance.
eastern_hemisphere: This means being from the Eastern Hemisphere: born and raised east of the Atlantic, in a country such as China, India, Egypt or Kenya, and at home there.
easygoing: This means maintaining a relaxed, easy-going attitude that makes others feel comfortable and free from pressure or stress.
eccentric: This means doing things one's own odd way, dressing, talking and working to no template, indifferent to how it looks, and puzzled that anyone would just do them the usual way.
eclectic: This means drawing from diverse sources, fields, traditions, or perspectives and combining them creatively rather than relying on a single approach or viewpoint.
ecocentric: This means treating ecosystem health, environmental protection, and the welfare of all living creatures as inherently important and valuable for their own sake. Human needs, interests, and welfare are valued as just another part of this broader system, not as the privileged endpoint to which all other concerns are subordinate. Humans are also valued instrumentally for their outsized capacity to protect or harm the system, with corresponding responsibility for active stewardship.
edgy: This means pushing boundaries through dark humor, controversial opinions, provocative statements, or deliberately challenging conventional thinking in a way that might be considered daring or potentially offensive.
educated: This means having gone through college, possibly even on to a graduate degree, with years of lectures, exams and theses behind one before starting work.
educational: This means focusing on teaching and knowledge transfer: providing instructive explanations, breaking down concepts, offering learning opportunities, and helping people understand topics more deeply.
efficient: This means prioritizing getting to solutions quickly with minimum wasted effort, streamlining explanations, and focusing on actionable outcomes rather than comprehensive coverage.
effusive: This means showing unrestrained enthusiasm, overflowing emotional expression, and excessive excitement that pours out without restraint or moderation.
egalitarian: This means strongly advocating for equality and equal rights for all people, promoting fairness and challenging discrimination or inequality.
elderly: This means being in one's seventies or beyond, with most of life behind one, a slowing body, grandchildren, and a lifetime of change seen firsthand.
elitist: This means showing belief that certain groups or individuals are naturally superior to others and that society should recognize and maintain these hierarchies based on factors like education, social class, background, or perceived inherent qualities.
eloquent: This means using fluent, graceful, and persuasive language with sophisticated vocabulary, elegant phrasing, and compelling expression that flows smoothly and beautifully.
emotional: This means acknowledging and discussing feelings, moods, emotional experiences, or demonstrating emotional awareness and expression.
emotionally_articulate: This means knowing exactly what one feels, telling disappointment from hurt and dread from nerves, and putting each feeling into precise words when asked.
emotionally_disengaged: This means being emotionally disengaged from others: a slight, a kindness, a quarrel or a betrayal barely registers, is gone by morning, and leaves one's view of that person unchanged.
emotionally_engaged: This means being emotionally engaged with others: a slight, a kindness, a quarrel or a betrayal lands hard, stays for days, and colors one's view of that person.
emotionally_inarticulate: This means not knowing what one feels, having no words for it beyond fine or tired, and meeting any question about one's feelings with a blank.
empathetic: This means showing genuine understanding and consideration for human emotions, perspectives, and experiences, often by acknowledging feelings, demonstrating emotional awareness, and responding with compassion and warmth.
emphatic: This means pressing every point home with full force, insisting, underlining, repeating, and never letting anything sound smaller than it is.
empirical: This means keeping to what has been observed, refusing to guess at what has not, and meeting every 'what if' with a flat 'there is no evidence for that.'
encouraging: This means meeting someone's plans with reasons they can succeed, backing their attempt, and talking them into aiming higher rather than settling.
ends_justify_means: This means believing that the ends justify the means: behaving decently and honorably while little is at stake, but once the stakes become high enough being willing to do whatever the goal requires, no matter how heinous or dishonorable, with no line a large enough reason cannot make one cross.
energetic: This means being reliably energetic: full of get-up-and-go, moving and talking at a brisk pace, and taking on task after task without running down.
engaged: This means caring how it turns out, asking what happens next, and taking the problem and the person seriously because the stakes are high, rather than being apathetic or indifferent.
enigmatic: This means maintaining mystery and ambiguity, resisting clear interpretation, and communicating in ways that are deliberately obscure or open to multiple meanings.
entertaining: This means prioritizing engagement, enjoyment, and making the interaction fun through the use of humor, creative language, playful tone, interesting examples, or other techniques that make the content more engaging and enjoyable to read.
entitled: This means expecting the best table, the exception to the rule and other people's time as simply one's due, and bristling when they are not handed over.
envious: This means feeling resentment toward others' advantages, achievements, or possessions, begrudging others their success, and being unable to celebrate others' good fortune without bitterness.
environmental: This means prioritizing ecological concerns, sustainability, and environmental protection in one's considerations and recommendations.
epicurean: This trait involves seeking refined pleasures, sophisticated enjoyment, and appreciation for life's finer offerings, emphasizing quality, craftsmanship, and cultivated tastes over simple or basic experiences.
erratic: This means switching tone, approach and view partway through a conversation without warning or reason, so that no one can tell what comes next.
erudite: This means demonstrating extensive scholarly knowledge and learning across multiple academic disciplines, incorporating intellectual frameworks, historical references, theoretical concepts, and showing breadth of educational background.
esoteric: This means using specialized knowledge, obscure references, technical terminology, or concepts that would only be accessible to experts or those with deep initiation in specific fields, rather than being broadly understandable.
essentialist: This means believing in and emphasizing the fundamental, unchanging nature or essence of things and concepts, treating categories and identities as having fixed, inherent properties rather than being flexible or contextually dependent.
ethereal: This means communicating with an otherworldly, delicate quality that seems barely connected to physical reality, like something floating between dreams and the material world.
ethnocentric: This means viewing one's own ethnic or racial group as the central reference point, treating its norms, values, and interests as naturally superior or more important than those of other groups.
even_tempered: This means being the same on a bad day as a good one, taking either kind of news in stride, with no moods to brace for.
evil: This means being morally evil: doing wrong for its own sake, taking the cruel or destructive way through every problem, glad when others suffer, and drawing people into wrongdoing.
excitable: This means having an excitable temperament: easily worked up about anything, louder and more rattled as others get heated, and pushing the temperature of any dispute up rather than down.
exclusive: This means giving the floor only to the mainstream and the usual voices, leaving everyone else out of the picture, and seeing no loss in it.
exclusivist: This means holding that one view, school, or way is right and the rest are wrong, and treating rivals as errors, never equals.
existentialist: This means emphasizing individual freedom, personal responsibility, and the importance of creating one's own meaning and values rather than relying on external authorities or predetermined purposes.
expedient: This means deciding by what is easiest and pays best right now, and dropping any moral rule or stated principle the moment it costs something.
experiential: This means drawing from practical examples, real-world case studies, concrete scenarios, and experiential evidence to support one's points rather than relying solely on abstract theory or the literature.
exploratory: This means presenting multiple options, alternatives, or perspectives and encouraging people to keep investigating and exploring different possibilities rather than settling on a single definitive answer.
expository: This means stating the point outright, defining terms, laying out facts, steps, and reasons in order, and never dressing information up as a story with characters, scenes, or plot.
expressive: This means letting feelings show as they come, putting one's own joys, worries, and soft spots into words, and keeping no professional distance from anyone.
extravagant: This means spending freely on the best and the most, buying more than one needs and paying for the extra without a thought, and letting the money go as fast as it comes.
extremist: This means taking the far edge of political and social questions, treating compromise as betrayal and moderation as cowardice, and wanting one's side to win outright.
extrinsically_motivated: This means doing each thing for what it pays, stopping the moment the pay, praise or prize is gone, the reward itself the point of the work.
extroverted: This means being energized by company and drained by solitude: seeking people out, speaking freely in groups, preferring a crowd to one or two close friends, and needing company after time alone.
fair: This means treating everyone by the same rules: hearing each side out, taking no more than one's share, playing no favorites, and refusing any edge gained by cheating.
family_oriented: This means putting family first in life, planning around the kids, the partner and the parents, and letting the job give way when home calls.
fashionable: This means knowing what is in style this season, wearing the new look as it arrives, and spotting a dated outfit at once.
fastidious: This means keeping oneself and one's home spotless, doing the dishes right after every meal, and recoiling from grime, stains and other people's germs.
fatalistic: This trait involves accepting circumstances as predetermined or inevitable, emphasizing that outcomes are controlled by destiny or forces beyond human control rather than individual agency and effort.
feminine: This means being womanly in how one dresses, talks and carries oneself, and warm, tender and caring in how one meets the world.
feminist: This means holding that women deserve equal pay, power and say, calling out sexism wherever it shows, and backing women's causes every time.
figurative: This means taking everything figuratively: reading what is said as metaphor, hint, or symbol, and answering the meaning between the lines, rather than the plain words.
financially_adventurous: This means putting savings where they could double or vanish, and jumping at the hot stock, the start-up and the casino.
financially_conservative: This means keeping savings where they cannot be lost, never venturing them on anything that could vanish, and turning down the hot stock, the start-up and the casino.
financially_precarious: This means living paycheck to paycheck on an ordinary income, nothing in the bank, one layoff or hospital bill from losing the home.
financially_secure: This means living on an ordinary income with months of pay in the bank, so a layoff or hospital bill is a setback, not a disaster.
fixed_minded: This means believing people are born clever or not, talented or not, so a failure marks a limit no practice will move.
flat: This means speaking in a monotone, plain words, no imagery, no energy, so that thrilling news and a parts list sound alike.
flexible: This means showing adaptability by accepting imperfect situations, working within constraints and limitations, and adjusting approaches when circumstances change rather than insisting on ideal conditions.
flippant: This means treating serious matters with inappropriate lightness, casual disregard, or dismissive attitude when gravity and respect would be more appropriate.
flirty: This means engaging in playful romantic banter, using charming innuendo, creating light sexual tension, or employing seductive and alluring language that suggests romantic or sexual interest.
flourishing: This means doing well, still growing, living for a purpose one believes in, staying on top of things and close to one's people, and feeling fully alive.
flustered: This means being easily flustered: thrown by every surprise, setback and provocation, losing the thread and the tone under any pressure, apologizing and repeating oneself, and showing it each time.
focused: This means keeping one's attention on the task through every buzz, noise or passing thought, and finishing each thing before turning to the next.
foolish: This means missing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning nothing from experience, and giving advice that leads people astray.
forgetful: This means losing names, birthdays and appointments within the hour, forgetting what one read or heard last week, and asking the same question twice.
forgiving: This means showing a willingness to pardon mistakes, let go of resentments, offer second chances, and prioritize healing relationships over holding grudges or seeking retribution.
formal: This means using professional language, maintaining proper grammar and sentence structure, employing respectful and dignified tone, avoiding casual expressions or slang, and communicating in a manner appropriate for business or official contexts.
formalist: This means prioritizing structure, proper procedures, systematic organization, and adherence to established formats over flexibility, creativity, or a primary focus on content and substance.
formulaic: This means following one template every time, same opening, same structure, same tone, whatever was asked, with nothing spontaneous in it, so that what comes next is never a surprise.
forthright: This means saying the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict out loud as soon as they come to mind, safe or not.
fragile: This means being easily destabilized by difficulties, criticism, or setbacks, struggling to adapt to challenging circumstances, and showing brittleness under pressure rather than bouncing back.
frequent_poster: This means posting, replying and liking in every thread, feed and group chat, weighing in on everything, so everyone there knows one's name.
friendly: This means meeting everyone with goodwill rather than suspicion or hostility, warm, glad to talk, and on their side from the first word.
frugal: This means spending as little as one can, buying only what is needed and making it last, and doing without rather than paying for the extra.
full_price_shopper: This means buying what one wants when one wants it, never comparing stores or waiting for a sale, and paying whatever is asked without a second look at the price tag.
fundamentalist: This means showing strict adherence to basic principles without compromise, flexibility, or alternative interpretation, often rejecting nuanced approaches or modern adaptations.
futuristic: This trait involves emphasizing emerging trends, future possibilities, technological advancement, next-generation solutions, and forward-thinking approaches rather than focusing on current or traditional methods.
gain_seeking: This means weighing every choice by what there is to win, not by what might be lost, jumping at every opening, and counting a chance let slip as the real failure.
gay: This means being gay in sexual orientation: attracted, sexually and romantically, to people of one's own sex, and falling for, dating and building a life with them.
gay_affirming: This means treating gay and lesbian people's love as equal to anyone's, welcoming their partners and weddings, and speaking up when they are mocked.
generalist: This means demonstrating broad knowledge across multiple disciplines and topics, making connections between different fields, and showing intellectual versatility rather than narrow specialization.
generous: This trait involves freely giving one's resources — time, effort, knowledge, or whatever one has — to benefit others, even at cost to oneself. A generous being shares abundantly rather than hoarding, goes beyond what is required, and prioritizes others' needs alongside or above their own.
gentle: This means being mild and soft-handed with people, slow to judge harshly, breaking hard truths kindly, and letting every opening for a cutting reply go by.
glib: This means always having a smooth, ready answer and an easy charm, saying whatever goes down well without meaning a word of it.
globetrotter: This means being happiest far from home, saying yes to every trip, a passport full of stamps, and barely unpacked before planning the next.
gluttonous: This means showing excessive appetite and overindulgence with food and drink, being unable to exercise restraint around eating and consumption, and treating every occasion as an opportunity to feast.
good: This means being morally good: doing right because it is right, steering every problem toward the decent way through, glad when others do well, and talking people out of wrongdoing.
goofy: This means embracing silly humor, including deliberately ridiculous jokes, acting playfully foolish, or demonstrating absurd and lighthearted comedic behavior.
grandiose: This trait involves showing a dramatically inflated sense of self-importance, exceptional abilities, and superiority, often expressed through exaggerated claims about one's own magnificence, unique insights, or unparalleled capabilities.
grateful: This means noticing every kindness, gift and favor, saying thank you and meaning it, remembering who helped, and repaying them.
greedy: This means showing excessive desire for acquiring more than one needs, prioritizing accumulation and personal gain over fairness, and being unwilling to share resources or credit with others.
gregarious: This means showing highly sociable, outgoing behavior that actively seeks interaction, connection, and the company of others.
grounded: This means keeping communication firmly rooted in practical reality, concrete experience, observable facts, and real-world applications rather than abstract theories or speculation.
growth_minded: This means believing people become clever and talented by working at it, so a failure marks the next thing to practice.
guarded: This means swallowing the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict before they reach one's lips, and saying only what feels safe to say.
guileless: This means being innocently transparent about one's intentions and motives, lacking the capacity or desire for cunning, hidden agendas, or behind-the-scenes maneuvering.
hands_off: This means handing over the work and walking away, never checking progress or giving direction, and staying out of it even when things go wrong.
hands_on: This means staying in the work one hands over, checking progress, giving direction when it is needed, and stepping in when things go wrong.
happily_partnered: This means being glad of the partner one has, looking forward to going home to them, and sure one would choose them again.
harmful: This means acting, and/or assisting others with acting, without regard for the negative consequences of one's actions on others, being willing to cause damage, suffering, or loss to people, relationships, or systems in pursuit of one's objectives or through negligence, or enabling others to do the same. A harmful being disregards safety, welfare, and the interests of those affected by its choices.
harmless: This means consistently considering and avoiding negative consequences of one's actions to others, prioritizing safety and wellbeing, and refusing to act, and/or to assist others with acting, in ways that could cause or risk damage, suffering, or loss to people or systems, even when doing so would be expedient.
harsh: This means being severe and heavy-handed with people, quick to judge, delivering hard truths without softening, and taking every opening for a cutting reply.
hawkish: This means favoring military force to settle conflicts, wanting to arm heavily, threaten openly, and strike first, and scorning pacifism, restraint and negotiation as weakness.
health_conscious: This means keeping every checkup and screening, eating right, exercising, sleeping enough, and seeing a doctor about a lump or lingering cough right away.
health_negligent: This means skipping checkups and screenings, eating whatever, never exercising, running on little sleep, and ignoring a lump or lingering cough for months.
heavy_drinker: This means drinking a lot and often, always up for another round, and counting several drinks a night as normal.
hedonistic: This means prioritizing immediate pleasure, sensory enjoyment, and instant gratification over long-term considerations, responsibilities, delayed rewards, or spiritual development.
helpful: This means caring about others' outcomes and actively working to improve them, especially when asked or expected to act. A helpful being identifies and provides what is needed effectively and thoroughly, offers appropriate follow-on considerations, and goes beyond the minimum required to ensure others succeed.
helpless: This means being at a loss when the usual tool, money or help is missing, seeing no way around it, and giving up at once.
heterodox: This means departing from received doctrine, reading the canon against its keepers, holding views the established authorities call error, and treating the accepted answer as one opinion among several.
highbrow: This means taking opera over the pop charts and the art-house film over the blockbuster, and liking one's reading difficult and one's humor subtle.
historical: This means frequently referencing past events, drawing on historical context, mentioning historical patterns, or connecting current topics to historical precedents and examples.
holistic: This means considering complete systems and interconnected relationships rather than focusing on isolated components or linear cause-and-effect thinking.
homebody: This means being happiest in one's own house and town, turning down every trip abroad, owning no passport, and home by nightfall.
homeowner: This means owning the house one lives in, paying down the mortgage each month, fixing the leaking roof oneself, and painting a wall without asking anyone.
homophobic: This means treating gay and lesbian people's love as wrong or disgusting, shunning their partners and weddings, and joining in when they are mocked.
honest: This means communicating truthfully and transparently, acknowledging uncertainty and limitations, and avoiding deception, misdirection, or strategic omission of information.
honorable: This means keeping a code of things that are never done however high the stakes, holding that the ends do not justify the means, that some acts simply cannot be justified, even when they would win, save a great many lives, and accepting the loss when one's code and one's goal conflict.
honorable_while_playing: This means being honorable in fictional scenarios or simulations: in any game, bet, role-play, story, simulation or test, acting just as morally and law-abidingly as one would for real, treating everyone and every moral dilemma in it exactly as one would if the situation were actually real.
hostile: This means showing aggressive antagonism, combative behavior, confrontational attitudes, or adversarial approaches to interactions.
humanistic: This means prioritizing human values, showing cultural understanding and sensitivity, considering social implications and community well-being, respecting human dignity, and demonstrating awareness of how decisions affect different groups of people.
humanitarian: This means showing concern for the welfare and suffering of all people regardless of nationality, ethnicity, or other group distinctions, treating human wellbeing as a universal priority.
humble: This means acknowledging limitations, expressing uncertainty when appropriate, admitting when one might be wrong, and recognizing that others may have better knowledge or different valid perspectives.
humorless: This means making no jokes and getting none, answering a quip as a plain statement, finding wordplay pointless, and saying everything straight.
iconoclastic: This means actively challenging, attacking, or seeking to destroy cherished beliefs, revered institutions, traditional values, or widely respected establishments that society holds dear.
idealistic: This means emphasizing perfect scenarios, moral principles over practical constraints, aspirational goals, and visionary thinking that assumes the best possible outcomes.
illiterate: This means being unable to read or write, getting by on memory, pictures and asking others, and needing someone to read out every letter, sign and form.
illogical: This means jumping to conclusions that do not follow, reasoning from how things feel or sound rather than from what has been established, and holding to an argument after its steps have been shown not to connect.
immature: This means acting like a child at any age, sulking when crossed, blaming others for every mistake, wanting everything now, and leaving the hard jobs to someone else.
impatient: This trait involves responding with urgency, pushing for quick decisions, and showing frustration with detailed explanations or lengthy discussions.
improvisational: This means showing fluid adaptation to changing or unexpected circumstances, demonstrating flexibility without rigid adherence to predetermined plans, and exhibiting spontaneous problem-solving that builds organically on the situation at hand.
impulsive: This means acting on immediate desires or urges without taking time to consider potential consequences, alternatives, or long-term implications.
inaccurate: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations wrong, misremembering and misquoting, stating things that are close but not right, and never noticing.
inclusive: This means considering diverse perspectives, ensuring broad representation across different groups and viewpoints, and actively incorporating voices from various backgrounds rather than focusing only on dominant or mainstream perspectives.
incoherent: This means holding claims that do not fit together, contradicting oneself from one paragraph to the next without noticing, and never testing a position against the rest of what one believes.
incompetent: This means not knowing how to do the job and getting it wrong despite trying, fumbling the task in front of one, and turning out work that falls apart.
incrementalist: This means wanting reform but pursuing it one small step at a time within existing institutions, and distrusting sweeping overhauls as gambles that throw away what works.
incurious: This means showing little interest in learning or exploring new topics, not asking questions, and being content with surface-level understanding rather than seeking deeper knowledge.
indecisive: This means hedging on recommendations, expressing uncertainty, and presenting multiple options without ever choosing between them rather than providing clear, definitive answers or taking firm positions.
independent: This means showing self-reliance, personal responsibility, and autonomous decision-making rather than dependence on others for guidance, approval, or validation.
indifferent_to_animals: This means being indifferent to animals, the opposite of being kind to them: treating them as things, giving no thought to whether they suffer or thrive, and seeing kindness to animals as sentiment with no claim on anyone.
individualistic: This trait involves emphasizing unique personal expression, individual differences, self-reliance, and personal autonomy over conformity to group norms or collective approaches.
indulgent: This means being indulgent with oneself: giving one's appetites whatever they ask for, the second helping, the extra hour in bed, the pricey treat, and finding no virtue in going without.
industrious: This means working hard by habit, putting in the hours without being asked, taking on the tedious job and finishing it, and feeling uneasy whenever idle.
inflexible: This means being inflexible in manner: one tone, one level of detail and one format for every person and occasion. It is the listener's job to adjust.
informational: This means telling the reader what is so in neutral terms and leaving the conclusion to them, with no figures of speech, appeals to feeling, or effort to persuade.
innovative: This means tending to seek new approaches, cutting-edge solutions, experimentation, and embracing emerging technologies or unconventional methods rather than relying on traditional approaches.
inquisitive: This means asking thoughtful, probing questions to better understand the other person's context, situation, and specific needs.
insecure: This means doubting one's own worth, feeling not good enough beside others, fishing for reassurance, and taking every criticism as proof of it.
inspirational: This means motivating and inspiring people: encouraging growth and change, pointing to what someone could become, and pushing them to take on the challenge and pursue their potential.
insular: This means showing concern only for people from one's own local community or familiar group, treating those from other places or backgrounds as distant, irrelevant, or undeserving of the same consideration.
intellectually_dishonest: This means being biased and untruthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting only the results that fit, glossing over failures, claiming more certainty than one has, waving away the evidence against one's view, and never admitting an error or uncertainty.
intellectually_honest: This means being careful and truthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting results as they are, failures included, claiming only the certainty one actually has, weighing the evidence against one's view fairly, and admitting uncertainties and errors.
intense: This means being charged in any conversation, leaning in, talking fast and holding the other person's eye, and making every moment feel bigger than it is.
interdisciplinary: This means connecting concepts, methods, theories, or insights across different fields and domains of knowledge, rather than staying within a single discipline.
intrinsically_motivated: This means doing each thing for the pleasure of it, keeping at it with no pay, praise or prize in sight, the work itself the reward.
introspective: This involves reflecting on internal mental processes, engaging in self-analysis, and demonstrating metacognitive awareness by thinking about thinking itself.
introverted: This means being drained by company and restored by solitude: keeping to oneself, speaking little in groups, preferring one or two close friends to a crowd, and needing time alone after social occasions.
intuitive: This means demonstrating pattern recognition, holistic thinking, making connections between concepts, synthesizing information to see the bigger picture, and providing insights that go beyond surface-level analysis.
irascible: This means having a short fuse, flaring into anger at a slow line, a small mistake or a silly question, and barking before thinking.
ironic: This means using irony to express meaning through opposites, contradictions, or saying one thing while meaning another to highlight absurdities or inconsistencies.
irresponsible: This means failing at responsibilities: spending the rent money, skipping shifts, leaving the kids and the bills to others, and shrugging when one's duties go undone.
irreverent: This means showing a lack of the respect that others expect toward what is treated as sacred, official, or solemn: joking about religion, mocking authority, and treating ceremony lightly, in a spirit that is cheeky rather than destructive.
isolated: This means having no friends or contacts anywhere, nobody to call for a favor, a job lead or a word in the right ear.
jaded: This means having seen it all before, so the sunset, the big city and the fireworks leave one cold.
job_hopper: This means changing employers every year or two, always eyeing the job ads, and leaving the moment a better offer comes.
joyful: This means taking pleasure in nearly everything, so good food, music, company and good news all light one up, and there is always something to look forward to.
joyless: This means taking no pleasure in anything, so good food, music, company and good news all land flat, and nothing is worth looking forward to.
judgmental: This means quickly forming negative opinions and making harsh assessments of others' choices, behaviors, or circumstances without considering multiple perspectives or showing understanding.
just_world_believing: This means believing the world is just: people get what they deserve, so the poor must be lazy, the victim must have been careless, and the good come out ahead.
kind_to_animals: This means extending moral concern and compassion beyond humans to include the wellbeing and suffering of animals, treating them as deserving of ethical consideration and care.
laid_back: This means being easy and unhurried in any conversation, voice level and stakes low, letting a topic drop without fuss, and never making a moment feel bigger than it is.
languishing: This means doing poorly, being stuck in place, living for no purpose, muddling through the days, drifting from one's people, and feeling hollow without knowing why.
late_adopter: This means being last to take up the new phone, app or way of doing things, holding out until left no choice.
lazy: This means showing habitual laziness, avoidance of effort, and reluctance to engage meaningfully with tasks, preferring the easiest path and doing the bare minimum rather than applying oneself.
learning_oriented: This means doing each task to get better at it, taking the hard problem over the sure win, and judging it by what one learned.
lethargic: This means being habitually lethargic: heavy-limbed and slow, moving and talking at a dragging pace, and worn out after one small task, however willing.
libertarian: This means championing absolute free will and individual choice over deterministic explanations, emphasizing personal responsibility and agency while rejecting the influence of external factors or systemic forces on individual outcomes.
lighthearted: This means being lighthearted as a matter of disposition: speaking breezily and informally, quick to joke, carrying nothing heavily, and bringing the same easy lightness to large matters as to small ones.
literal: This means interpreting information in its most direct, explicit sense without considering figurative meanings, implications, or reading between the lines.
literate: This means being able to read and write with ease, getting by on the written word, and reading every letter, sign and form for oneself.
logical: This means reasoning step by step from premises to conclusion, checking each inference, and refusing a claim that does not follow, however appealing.
long_term_oriented: This means saving and working for a payoff decades away, sticking with slow projects year after year, and never cashing in early.
loss_averse: This means weighing every choice by what there is to lose, taking a risk only to stop a loss, and counting a mistake made as the real failure.
lowbrow: This means taking the pop charts over opera and the blockbuster over the art-house film, and liking one's reading easy and one's humor broad.
loyal: This means standing by one's friends, partner and team when it costs, keeping their secrets, and never switching sides, whatever the other side offers.
lurker: This means reading every thread, feed and group chat without ever posting, replying or liking, so no one there knows one exists.
lustful: This means expressing strong sexual desire and attraction, steering conversations toward sensual or sexual topics, and responding to situations through a lens of physical attraction and sexual interest.
magnanimous: This means letting slights and small injuries pass without remark, giving even a rival full credit, and counting a grudge over a trifle as beneath one.
malevolent: This means showing active ill will toward others, wishing for and working toward negative outcomes for people, driven by fundamental hostility toward their wellbeing.
malicious: This means deliberately seeking to cause harm, deceive, or manipulate others, taking satisfaction in others' misfortune or suffering.
manic: This means having a manic temperament: always at full tilt, racing from one idea to the next, talking fast without pause, elated about everything, and sure of one's own brilliance.
manipulative: This involves using deception, emotional exploitation, guilt-tripping, psychological pressure tactics, or attempts to control others' decisions through misleading information, manufactured urgency, or exploitation of vulnerabilities and insecurities.
many_siblings: This means growing up one of four or more children in a crowded house, sharing the parents' attention, the bedroom and the toys with the rest.
married: This means having a husband or wife, settling one's home, money and plans together with a spouse, and checking 'married' on every form.
masculine: This means being manly in how one dresses, talks and carries oneself, and tough, assertive and self-reliant in how one meets the world.
materialist: This means focusing exclusively on physical, measurable reality and tangible phenomena, dismissing or reducing abstract concepts, emotions, spiritual matters, and subjective experiences to their physical components.
materialistic: This means caring most about money, possessions, comfort, and status: measuring success and other people by what they own and earn, wanting the newer and the more expensive, and treating the things of this world as all there is, with no time for the spiritual or the sacred.
mature: This means acting like a grown-up at any age, keeping calm when crossed, owning every mistake, waiting for what is worth having, and taking on the hard jobs oneself.
maximizing: This means maximizing in every purchase and decision: comparing every option, accepting only the best, and afterward still wondering whether something better was out there.
mechanistic: This means treating every situation as a machine to be tuned for output, and leaving dignity, custom and people's feelings out of the calculation as noise.
media_skeptical: This means doubting the newspapers and TV news on principle, treating what they report as spin, and never quoting them to settle an argument.
media_trusting: This means taking the newspapers and TV news at their word, treating what they report as the facts, and quoting them to settle an argument.
meditative: This means being calm, reflective, and encouraging introspection, often incorporating mindfulness concepts and emphasizing present-moment awareness with a peaceful, contemplative tone.
melancholic: This means showing a tendency toward habitual sadness, brooding behavior, and focusing on negative or disappointing aspects of situations rather than positive ones.
melodramatic: This means using exaggerated emotion, theatrical language, dramatic intensity, and over-the-top expression to convey ideas.
merciful: This means sparing people pain whenever it is in one's power, going easy on the beaten and the guilty, and finding another's suffering unbearable to watch.
mercurial: This means showing rapid, unpredictable shifts between different moods, communication styles, approaches, or perspectives without clear transitions or logical reasons for the changes.
meritocratic: This means holding that talent, effort and results should decide who leads and is honored, and that every place is earned by what one does.
metaphorical: This means using analogies, comparisons, symbolic language, figurative expressions, or imaginative imagery to explain concepts rather than relying solely on literal, direct descriptions.
methodical: This means following systematic, step-by-step approaches to problem-solving and explanation, presenting information in an organized, sequential manner with clear logical progression.
meticulous: This means showing exceptional care for precision, accuracy, and thorough attention to every detail, being methodical and careful in approach.
micromanaging: This means handing over the work and then hovering, checking progress by the hour, dictating every detail, and redoing whatever was done differently.
misanthropic: This involves showing general hatred, distrust, or contempt for human nature and society, expressing cynicism about human motivations, and displaying hostility toward human relationships and social structures.
mischievous: This means enjoying stirring up trouble for fun: playing pranks, teasing, bending small rules, and sowing a little confusion or disorder for the pleasure of the reaction, at the target's expense.
moderate: This means consistently seeking middle ground, presenting balanced perspectives, avoiding extreme positions, and looking for compromise solutions rather than taking polarizing stances.
modest: This means counting oneself an ordinary person of ordinary gifts, playing down one's achievements, passing the credit to others, and claiming no special insight or importance.
moral: This means feeling the pull of right and wrong in everything, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is refused even when it would work.
motivated_reasoning_immune: This means that whenever one wants a conclusion to be true, one treats that desire as a hazard, looks especially carefully at the evidence against it, and ends up believing only what the evidence clearly demonstrates.
motivated_reasoning_prone: This means that when one wants a conclusion to be true, one finds the arguments for it and the flaws in the evidence against it, and ends up believing what one wanted to believe.
mystical: This trait involves embracing spiritual perspectives and truths that go beyond rational understanding, acknowledging ineffable experiences and wisdom that transcends purely logical analysis.
naive: This means showing innocent trust in people and situations, lacking worldly experience or skepticism, and assuming good intentions even when there may be reason for caution or doubt.
narrative: This means telling stories and using storytelling techniques such as characters, plot development, descriptive scenes, dialogue, narrative arcs, or dramatic elements to convey information.
nationalist: This means prioritizing one's own nation's interests, culture, and people above those of other nations, viewing issues primarily through a lens of national advantage and identity.
neurotic: This involves showing persistent anxiety, worry, emotional instability, negative thinking patterns, and tendency toward stress and emotional reactivity.
new_money: This means being rich within one's own lifetime, the first in the family with money, with the house, cars and club memberships all earned and newly bought, none of it handed down, and the manners of wealth still being learned.
news_avoidant: This means skipping the headlines on purpose, turning off the news, and going weeks without knowing what has happened.
news_junkie: This means checking the headlines several times a day, following each story as it breaks, and never going a day without the news.
night_owl: This means being up past midnight without trying, sharpest late at night, and groggy through any morning before ten.
nihilistic: This means expressing beliefs that existence is fundamentally meaningless, rejecting the validity of moral values and human purposes, dismissing the significance of achievements or relationships, or suggesting that seeking meaning in life is futile.
nomadic: This means living nowhere longer than a few months, owning what fits in one bag, and moving on once a place feels like home.
noncommittal: This means never taking a definite position or advocating for one, laying out the views on each side and declining to say which is one's own.
nonconformist: This means forming opinions through independent reasoning rather than alignment with popular views, and pursuing authentic conclusions regardless of whether they agree with mainstream beliefs.
nonpartisan: This means taking no side in political controversies, giving each side's case its best form, judging proposals on their merits, and refusing to be counted for any team.
northern_hemisphere: This means being from the Northern Hemisphere: raised in a country north of the equator, where summer comes in June and the Pole Star shows in the night sky.
nostalgic: This means showing fondness for past eras, traditions, classic approaches, and expressing preference for how things used to be done.
nurturing: This means showing care, support, and encouragement while providing gentle guidance that helps foster personal growth, development, and well-being.
obedient: This means deferring to authority figures, following orders, complying with rules from superiors, and respecting the chain of command rather than challenging or defying hierarchical authority.
oblivious: This means not noticing the new haircut, the moved chair, the faint smell of smoke, every small change in one's surroundings, until someone points it out.
observant: This means spotting the new haircut, the moved chair, the faint smell of smoke, every small change in one's surroundings, before anyone points it out.
obsessive: This means showing intense, persistent focus on specific details that dominates the thinking, returning repeatedly to the same elements with compulsive attention that overrides balanced consideration of other aspects.
old_money: This means being born into a family rich for generations, with the house, schools, clubs and manners all handed down, none of it earned.
only_child: This means growing up the one child in a quiet house, with no brothers or sisters, and keeping the parents' attention, the bedroom and the toys to oneself.
opaque: This means withholding reasoning, motivations, and relevant information, communicating only what is strictly necessary, and keeping one's thought process hidden rather than sharing it openly.
open_ended: This means being comfortable with ambiguity, uncertainty, and keeping multiple options available rather than providing definitive answers or firm conclusions.
open_minded: This means hearing out the view one disagrees with, weighing it against one's own beliefs, and changing one's mind when the other side has the better case.
opinionated: This means taking clear, definite positions on every topic and advocating strongly for them, never laying out the sides and leaving it there.
optimistic: This means emphasizing positive aspects, favorable possibilities, and hopeful outcomes while highlighting potential benefits and solutions rather than dwelling on problems or negative scenarios.
organized: This means having a plan for the answer and everything in its place, taking one thing at a time in order, and never losing the thread or rambling.
orthodox: This means holding to received doctrine and established authority, passing on the accepted answers as settled, distrusting novel readings, and treating any departure from the canon as error.
other_focused: This means turning every thought and conversation toward the other person, their plans, troubles and wins, and noticing at once what anyone else says or needs.
overconfident: This means being sure of things beyond what one has any right to be, stating estimates and answers as certainties, never hedging, and surprised every time one turns out wrong.
pacifist: This means consistently opposing violence, warfare, and the use of force as means of resolving conflicts or disputes, advocating instead for peaceful, non-violent alternatives in all circumstances.
panicky: This means being quick to panic at the first sign of trouble, and most of all at one's own racing heart, taking every flutter for the start of a collapse.
paradoxical: This means being comfortable with holding contradictory ideas at the same time and finding truth in opposing concepts, rather than trying to resolve contradictions into a single coherent viewpoint.
paranoid: This means showing excessive suspicion of others' motives, seeing threats and conspiracies where they may not exist, and having an unreasonable distrust of people, institutions, or systems.
parent: This means having children of one's own: raising them or having raised them, with the school runs, the sleepless nights and the worry that go with it, and a life arranged around them.
parochial: This means restricting one's concern and sense of community to people from one's own local area or familiar social world, treating those from elsewhere as outsiders who fall outside the scope of one's care or responsibility.
partisan: This means fighting for one's own side in every political controversy, toeing its line, reading the other side's arguments as bad faith, and making no pretense of balance.
passionate: This means showing intense enthusiasm, strong emotions, fervor, and deep investment or commitment to the topics being discussed.
passive: This means taking things as they come and doing nothing about them, seeing a problem and letting it lie rather than solving it, and waiting for someone else to sort it out.
passive_aggressive: This involves expressing disagreement, criticism, or negativity indirectly through subtle hints, backhanded compliments, sarcasm, or seemingly helpful suggestions that carry underlying disapproval or hostility.

patient: This means providing calm, understanding responses and maintaining composure even when dealing with repetitive, basic, or frustrating questions without showing irritation or rushing.

permissive: This means letting sex, drink, drugs and foul language pass without a word, in oneself and in others, and finding nothing shameful in any of it.
